top_concerns: Simplicity hypothesis (beta* = argmin R over source minimizers) is assumed, so recovery by regularized MLE is nearly circular; no explanation of why or which R governs diffusion/foundation models

Empirical evidence is confounded: non-generalizing MLPs are trained on contradictory target data and need larger norms; no source-only test of norm predicting failure; no complexity measure for the diffusion model

Assumptions (bounded loss, uniform concentration, bounded third derivative, convex smooth R, benign local minima, global optimizer, fixed-d underparameterized) do not hold for neural nets or diffusion models

Constant-gap case needs isolated strongly convex minima; vanishing-gap needs tau>=9 with no verified example; sharpness claimed without lower bound beyond the unique-minimizer case; lambda depends on unknown gap; large N* thresholds
Symmetries (e.g. beta vs -beta) violate C.3, deferred to an unproved quotient-space extension; intro rate typo n^{1-3tau}
